_note: Entities beyond Natural Earth's countries, plus overrides. kind: state | de facto state | dependency | armed group | international. 'base' remaps Natural Earth features whose de facto controller isn't the feature itself.

ATA.note: No state exercises sovereignty. Seven territorial claims are held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959), and research stations are operated by around 30 countries.

BRT.note: Terra nullius: claimed by neither Egypt nor Sudan, because each claims the Hala'ib Triangle instead under a different boundary line.

CNM.note: The UN buffer zone (Green Line) between the Republic of Cyprus and Northern Cyprus, patrolled by UNFICYP since 1974.

KAS.note: Held by India since 1984; claimed by Pakistan.

SPI.note: A stretch of the Chile-Argentina border that has never been demarcated.

PGA.note: Individual reefs and islands are occupied by China, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, and Taiwan.

SCR.note: Controlled by Chinese coast guard ships since a 2012 standoff; claimed by the Philippines.

BJN.note: Awarded to Colombia by the International Court of Justice in 2012.

SER.note: Awarded to Colombia by the International Court of Justice in 2012.

USG.note: Leased to the United States since 1903; Cuba considers the lease invalid.

KAB.note: Leased to Russia by Kazakhstan for the Baikonur Cosmodrome; administered by Russia until 2050.

ESB.note: A UK Sovereign Base Area retained when Cyprus became independent in 1960.

WSB.note: A UK Sovereign Base Area retained when Cyprus became independent in 1960.

BRI.note: A river island claimed by both Brazil and Uruguay.

SAH.name: Sahrawi Republic
SAH.recognition: Recognized by several dozen UN members and a member of the African Union; governs the area east of Morocco's berm.

TWN.name: Taiwan
TWN.recognition: Recognized by about a dozen UN members; claimed by the People's Republic of China.

KOS.recognition: Recognized by roughly half of UN members; claimed by Serbia.

CYN.name: Northern Cyprus
CYN.recognition: Recognized only by Turkey; claimed by Cyprus.

SOL.recognition: Self-governing since 1991; recognized by Israel in December 2025, and claimed by Somalia.

PSX.name: Palestine
PSX.recognition: Recognized by most UN members; a UN non-member observer state.

ABK.name: Abkhazia
ABK.recognition: Recognized by Russia and a handful of other states; claimed by Georgia.

SOS.name: South Ossetia
SOS.recognition: Recognized by Russia and a handful of other states; claimed by Georgia.

PMR.name: Transnistria
PMR.recognition: Recognized by no UN member; claimed by Moldova.

UNFICYP.name: UN Buffer Zone
UNFICYP.formal: United Nations Buffer Zone in Cyprus

AFG.note: Governed by the Taliban's Islamic Emirate since August 2021. Russia became the first state to recognize it, in July 2025.

MMR.note: Ruled by the military since the February 2021 coup; Min Aung Hlaing became president in 2026 after elections widely dismissed as neither free nor fair.

SDN.note: The army-led government, based in Port Sudan and Khartoum, at war with the Rapid Support Forces since April 2023.

LBY.note: The internationally recognized government in Tripoli; the east and south are held by Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army.

YEM.note: The internationally recognized government, based in Aden, backed by Saudi Arabia.

SOM.note: Federal government in Mogadishu, with the federal member states that cooperate with it.

TASIS.name: RSF-held Sudan
TASIS.recognition: Proclaimed by the Rapid Support Forces and allies in 2025; recognized by no state.
TASIS.note: The Rapid Support Forces paramilitary, at war with the army since April 2023.

SPLMN.name: SPLM-North (al-Hilu)
SPLMN.note: Has governed parts of the Nuba Mountains since 2011; allied with the RSF in the Tasis coalition since 2025.

SLMAW.name: SLM (Abdel Wahid)
SLMAW.formal: Sudan Liberation Movement / Army (Abdel Wahid al-Nur)
SLMAW.note: Holds parts of Jebel Marra and Tawila, neutral between the army and the RSF.

HOU.name: Houthi-held Yemen
HOU.recognition: Recognized by no state; Iran maintains relations.
HOU.note: The Houthi movement has held Sanaa since 2014 and governs most of Yemen's population.

LNA.name: Eastern Libya
LNA.formal: Government of National Stability / Libyan National Army
LNA.recognition: Recognized by no state; backed by Egypt, the UAE, and Russia.
LNA.note: Khalifa Haftar's forces have held the east since 2014 and most of the south since 2019.

SWD.name: Suwayda
SWD.formal: Druze administration of Jabal al-Arab (Jabal Bashan)
SWD.note: Druze factions under Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri have run the province outside government control since the July 2025 fighting.

HAMAS.name: Hamas-held Gaza
HAMAS.note: Hamas has governed Gaza since 2007; since the October 2025 ceasefire it holds the area west of the Israeli 'yellow line'.

M23.name: AFC/M23
M23.recognition: Recognized by no state; backed by Rwanda.
M23.note: Took Goma in January 2025 and Bukavu in February 2025 and runs a parallel administration in the Kivus.

PUNTLAND.name: Puntland
PUNTLAND.recognition: An autonomous federal member state that has refused to recognize the federal government since 2024; it does not claim independence.

JUBALAND.name: Jubaland
JUBALAND.recognition: Broke with the federal government in November 2024 and since December 2025 calls itself a government rather than a federal member state; it does not claim independence.

SHABAAB.name: al-Shabaab
SHABAAB.note: Al-Qaeda's Somali affiliate, which taxes and governs much of rural southern Somalia.

AA.name: Arakan Army
AA.formal: Arakan Army / United League of Arakan
AA.note: Took most of Rakhine State in 2024-25 and runs its own administration.

UWSA.name: Wa State
UWSA.formal: United Wa State Army / Wa State
UWSA.recognition: Recognized by no state; nominally part of Myanmar but self-governing since 1989, closely tied to China.

NDAA.name: Mongla
NDAA.note: A ceasefire group that has run Mongla autonomously since 1989.

MNDAA.name: Kokang
MNDAA.note: Retook Laukkai in January 2024 and Kutkai in March 2026.

TNLA.name: Ta'ang (TNLA)
TNLA.note: Holds Namhsan, Mantong, Namhkan and Namtu; returned Mogok, Kyaukme, Hsipaw and Nawnghkio to the junta under Chinese pressure.
